name: Cox's Bazar
description: The world's longest natural sea beach stretches about 120 km along the Bay of Bengal. It is the most popular seaside getaway for tourists in Bangladesh.

name: Kuakata
description: Known as the daughter of the sea, Kuakata offers a rare view of both sunrise and sunset over the Bay of Bengal. It is a quiet, traditional beach town.

name: Saint Martin
description: The only coral island in Bangladesh, located in the deep blue waters of the Bay of Bengal. It is famous for clear water, coral reefs and laid-back island life.

name: Bandarban
description: A scenic hill district with green valleys, rivers and the highest peaks in Bangladesh. It is a popular spot for trekking and nature lovers.

name: Sajek Valley
description: Often called the roof of Rangamati, Sajek Valley is famous for its clouds floating below the hills. It is a calm and beautiful hill retreat near the Mizoram border.

name: Khagrachari
description: A peaceful hill district known for its rolling green hills, indigenous culture and waterfalls. Alutila Cave is one of its most popular attractions.

name: Sundarbans
description: The largest mangrove forest in the world and home of the Royal Bengal Tiger. It spreads across Bangladesh and India along the Bay of Bengal coast.

name: Lawachara National Park
description: A tropical rainforest in Sylhet, famous for its tall trees, hanging vines and rare wildlife. It is one of the easiest forest getaways from Dhaka.

name: Sonargaon
description: Once the capital of Bengal, Sonargaon is a quiet old town near Dhaka full of Mughal ruins, a folk museum and riverside views.

name: Mahasthangarh
description: The ancient archaeological site of Pundranagar, one of the earliest urban centres in Bangladesh. Its old brick walls and ruins date back over 2,500 years.

name: Paharpur (Somapura Mahavihara)
description: A UNESCO World Heritage site and one of the great Buddhist monasteries of the Indian subcontinent. The huge central shrine is an icon of ancient Bengal.

name: Sreemangal
description: A small tea-growing town surrounded by lush green tea gardens. It is the tea capital of Bangladesh and known for its calm, slow village life.

name: Ratargul Swamp Forest
description: Often called the Sundarbans of Sylhet, this freshwater swamp forest fills with water in the monsoon season. Boating under the trees is a unique experience.

name: Jaflong
description: A scenic border town in Sylhet known for its stone collections, waterfalls and the Dawki river flowing from India. It has a calm rural charm.
